land.text: the British Solomon Islands Protectorate: 'declared the southern Solomon Islands a British protectorate' in 1893, with Rennell and Bellona, Sikaiana and the Santa Cruz Islands added in 1898-1899 and the Shortlands, Choiseul, Santa Isabel and Ontong Java in 1900

predecessors.note: Bougainville and Buka stayed German in 1900 and are now an autonomous region of Papua New Guinea ('does not form part of the nation of Solomon Islands'). Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row (1969-1995) still contains 78 of the country's 110 land cells in 1980, so the British dossier must hand the protectorate over in 1978.

capitals.name: Honiara
capitals.note: The page gives only the present capital ('Capital and largest city: Honiara 9°25′55″S 159°57′20″E'); no earlier capital or move is recorded in the pages opened.

correction.text: the Solomon Islands at independence on 7 July 1978: the former British Solomon Islands Protectorate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1979, a year after 'granted independence on 7 July 1978' (Solomon Islands page; History of Solomon Islands: 'Independence was granted on 7 July 1978').

correction.text: all the provinces the page names, from Temotu in the east to Western and Choiseul in the north-west; Bougainville is excluded ('does not form part of the nation of Solomon Islands')

keyframe_review.note: 37,719 km2 against the infobox 28,896 km2 (ratio 1.31, fine). The 109-vertex outline is simplified: at the gazetteer's grid it holds 80 land cells against 110 for the Natural Earth country polygon, leaving out cells in Western (8), Malaita (7), Choiseul (4), Isabel (4), Central (3), Guadalcanal (2), Rennell and Bellona (2) and Temotu (1). It correctly leaves out Bougainville. The country spec draws every island the page names.

correction.text: the whole archipelago, as for 1979-2023 (same outline in Cliopatria)

keyframe_review.note: Same outline and area as the 1979 shape; same correction.

region.text: the British Solomon Islands Protectorate (southern Solomons from 1893; Rennell and Bellona, Sikaiana, the Santa Cruz Islands and Anuta 1898-1899; the Shortlands, Choiseul, Santa Isabel and Ontong Java 1900)

ledger.note: 1978: the Solomon Islands become independent from the United Kingdom. Infobox 'from the United Kingdom: 7 July 1978'; 'granted independence on 7 July 1978' after full self-government in 1976. Bougainville, 'politically an autonomous region of Papua New Guinea', is not part of the state.

wars.name: Solomon Islands ethnic tension
wars.outcome: No territory changed hands. Honiara 'became a Malaitan enclave'; the MEF 'seized the parliament by force' on 5 June 2000; an international force (RAMSI) entered in August 2003 (July 2003 on the Solomon Islands page), Australia-led, at the government's request.
wars.note: The Solomon Islands page dates the IFM's campaign to late 1998 and the Malaita Eagle Force to mid-1999; the History page says violence 'erupted' in early 1999 and names the Honiara Peace Accord of 28 June 1999. The dedicated article could not be opened (Ethnic_violence_in_the_Solomon_Islands, URL not found). Neighbour commonwealth-of-australia led RAMSI; no occupation or contest zone is recorded because neither page names ground held.

certainty.note: Island coasts; maritime limits are not drawn. The northern limit with Papua New Guinea dates from 1900, when Britain received the northern Solomons 'minus Buka and Bougainville'; 'the two nations regularised border operations in a 2004 agreement'.

notes: Cliopatria rows. The Solomon Islands row starts 1979 but independence was 7 July 1978 (keyframe added). British Colonial Empire 1969-1995 still contains 78 of the 110 land cells in 1980, so the Solomons are drawn British until 1995; eu-11 should end it in 1978. The outline omits many island cells at the grid's resolution (see the 1979 verdict) and the keyframes use the country polygon. Pages: the dedicated tension article would not open (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_violence_in_the_Solomon_Islands, URL not found); History of Solomon Islands was opened instead. Disagreements: the Solomon Islands page gives both March and June 1893 for the protectorate and cites the 1899 Tripartite Convention for a 1900 transfer; RAMSI arrived in July (Solomon Islands page) or August 2003 (History page). The Pacific War (Tulagi occupied May 1942, Guadalcanal counter-invaded August 1942) is pre-state and belongs to the protectorate's dossier. Needed from other groups: British Solomon Islands Protectorate (1893-1978, suggested slug british-solomon-islands-protectorate) and, for the Anglo-German line, the German New Guinea dossier (oc-02-x).
